title: Set appetite instead of estimating infinity
principle: Ryan Singer’s Shape Up (public at basecamp.com/shapeup): decide how much time you’re willing to spend (appetite) before shaping a solution—fixed time, variable scope. Stops AI product chats from expanding into endless rebuilds.
procedure: Name the raw idea and the problem it claims to solve.
Set an appetite (e.g., small/medium cycle)—not an estimate of ‘true’ size.
Shape only what fits; list no-gos and rabbit holes.
Bet consciously; circuit-break if the build blows the appetite.
examplePrompts:
Shape this idea with appetite (Singer / Shape Up public book):
- Problem in one paragraph.
- Appetite: [2 days | 2 weeks | 6 weeks].
- Solution elements that fit; explicit no-gos.
- Rabbit holes to avoid.
Return a pitch outline—not a backlog.
We keep estimating ‘how long’. Flip to appetite: what would we build if we only had one week?
promptWhy: Appetite constrains scope before UI fantasy.
tips: Later Singer writing adds Framing vs Shaping—use when helpful.
No endorsement of Basecamp process as universal law.
